group.passage: Norway may seem an unlikely leader in clean transport. The small Nordic country, home to about 5.3 million people, has grown rich by selling oil and gas to the rest of the world. Yet on its own roads, it has gone further than any other nation in replacing petrol and diesel cars with electric ones. The change did not happen by chance. More than a decade ago, the government chose to make electric cars the easy option rather than to ban other cars. Buyers of electric models were spared the heavy import duties, registration fees, and sales taxes charged on petrol and diesel cars, including a 25 percent value added tax. Drivers were also excused from road tolls, given cheaper parking and ferry rides, and allowed to use bus lanes in crowded city centers. One energy expert believes that the high taxes on fuel-burning cars mattered most, while the other benefits simply made daily life more convenient. Charging was the next challenge. With an early push from the government and then money from private companies, Norway built nearly 8,000 fast-charging stations. At many newer petrol stations, drivers now see the chargers first and the pumps behind them. The results appear in the chart. In March 2019, electric cars outsold petrol and diesel cars in a single month for the first time, and the yearly share kept rising until almost every new car sold was electric. Norway had set a goal of ending sales of new petrol and diesel cars by 2025, and it came very close. Not everyone is satisfied. Some critics say the generous tax breaks mostly helped wealthy families and favored private cars over public transport. Now that electric cars dominate the market, the government has started to withdraw some of its support. Still, other countries are watching closely. Norway's experience suggests that a rapid switch is possible when policies stay in place long enough for people to trust them.

translation_zh.text:
挪威看起來似乎不太可能成為潔淨交通的領頭羊。這個人口約 530 萬的北歐小國，是靠著把石油和天然氣賣到世界各地而致富的。然而在自己國內的道路上，它比任何其他國家都走得更遠，用電動車取代汽油車和柴油車。

這個轉變並非偶然。十多年前，政府選擇讓電動車成為容易的選項，而不是禁止其他車輛。購買電動車的人不必繳納汽油車和柴油車要繳的高額進口關稅、登記費和銷售稅，其中包括 25% 的加值稅。駕駛人還免付道路通行費、享有較便宜的停車費和渡輪票價，並可在擁擠的市中心使用公車專用道。一位能源專家認為，對燃油車課徵的重稅才是最關鍵的因素，其他的好處只是讓日常生活更方便。

充電是下一個挑戰。在政府初期的推動、之後再由民間企業出資之下，挪威建造了將近 8,000 座快速充電站。在許多較新的加油站，駕駛人現在先看到的是充電樁，加油機反而在後面。

成果呈現在圖表中。2019 年 3 月，電動車在單月銷量中首度超越汽油車和柴油車，而每年的比例持續上升，直到幾乎每一輛售出的新車都是電動車。挪威曾設定在 2025 年以前停止銷售新的汽油車和柴油車的目標，而它已經非常接近這個目標。

並不是每個人都滿意。有些批評者說，優厚的減稅措施主要讓富裕家庭受惠，而且偏重私人汽車、忽略了大眾運輸。既然電動車已經主導市場，政府已開始撤回部分補助。不過，其他國家仍在密切觀察。挪威的經驗顯示，只要政策維持得夠久、讓民眾信任，快速轉換是做得到的。

【圖 1】新售汽車中電動車所占比例（2015–2025，%；電動車包含純電動車與插電式油電混合車），依序為 2015、2017、2019、2021、2023、2025 年：挪威 22、39、56、86、90、97；中國 1.1、2.4、5、16、38、53；全世界 0.68、1.4、2.7、9.3、18、25；美國 0.7、1.3、2.1、4.7、9.7、10。

事實單沒有的細節：“it has gone further than any other nation in replacing petrol and diesel cars with electric ones”——事實單只有 4 個地區的資料，CBC 寫 considered the world leader in EVs，說法屬實但未列入事實單。
事實單沒有的細節：“rather than to ban other cars”（第 1 題 D 的稽核證據句）——事實單沒有「不禁止燃油車」這一條；實情是挪威 2025 目標不具強制力、沒有禁售，說法正確，建議補進事實單。
details.method_zh: 逐句比對選文、圖表、題幹與選項中的事實與數字和事實單；圖表數值重新下載 OWID grapher CSV 比對；可開啟的來源（Smithsonian、NPR、C&EN、National Geographic、UW News、Science News、NOAA、CBC、Taipei Times、Focus Taiwan）逐條確認。
